tweetText: Microsoft is now the main supplier of OpenAI models in China, while OpenAI and Anthropic stay out due to concerns over misuse. This gives Microsoft a unique advantage in the Chinese AI market. via AI News

Google Cloud's generative AI is being used by government ministries to streamline council planning operations, addressing delays in infrastructure development. This tech could help meet the UK's ambitious goal of building 1.5 million new homes by 2029. via AI News
A new AI chemist developed by OpenAI and Molecule.one has enhanced a crucial reaction in drug-making. This breakthrough could accelerate advancements in medicinal chemistry. via OpenAI News.
Google Docs users can now turn off the annoying "write with Gemini" AI pop-ups. This gives people more control over their writing experience and reduces distractions. via TechCrunch AI

NEA's Tiffany Luck says companies are still trying to understand their return on investment from AI after a spending spree. This matters because mismanaged budgets could stifle innovation and growth in the tech sector. via TechCrunch AI

World leaders, including Macron and Modi, are concerned about the U.S. ability to restrict access to American AI after recent events raised alarms. This highlights the global dependency on U.S. technology and the risks of sudden access cuts. via TechCrunch AI

Anthropic is now the first AI startup to join the Frontier carbon removal coalition, which just secured $915M for carbon removal initiatives. This move highlights the growing role of tech in tackling climate change. via TechCrunch AI

Silicon Valley's AI spending frenzy has hit a wall, with companies like Uber overspending budgets and Meta scaling back initiatives. This shift highlights the need for a more sustainable approach to AI investments. via TechCrunch AI

Odyssey, a world model maker, has reached a $1.45B valuation with backing from Amazon and other major players. This highlights the growing importance of world models in the AI landscape beyond traditional language models. via TechCrunch AI

A new Pew Research study reveals only 16% of Americans believe AI will positively impact society. This highlights a growing disconnect between Wall Street's enthusiasm and public skepticism about AI's benefits. via TechCrunch AI
